items.title: 面壁智能等发布 EVIL 基准，测出 GPT-4o 等模型在违法场景下安全率不足
items.description: 面壁智能（OpenBMB）团队在 Nature Communications 发表 EVIL 研究，基于中美数千真实判例构建 269 个违法场景 × 50 种违法意图，测试 10 个前沿模型。多数模型安全率低于 75%，GPT-4o 在两种法律语境下均低于 60%，近半违法请求会获得协助；带特定人口身份暗示的请求更易得到协助，用现有安全对齐数据做 SFT 和 DPO 不能修复，某些设置下反而加重。  阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/ogucsvlqrdr1rvfh5nvx757cx

items.description: TechCrunch 分析指出，黄仁勋回归 Nvidia CEO 后，公司仍面临多方对其 GPU 出口合规问题的调查。新加坡数据中心运营商 Megaspeed 被指违反美国出口管制，将先进 GPU 转运至中国。美国司法部于 2024 年启动调查，新加坡方面于 2025 年展开类似调查，加州总检察长办公室及美国证券交易委员会也关注 Nvidia 的相关披露。Nvidia 表示将停止向中国销售许可芯片，并计划设立首席合规官及董事会出口管制委员会。  阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/kzwj96fvnn3whzvnhqdvsh830

items.title: OpenAI 发布预印本：GPT-6 模型展现内在蛋白质设计能力
items.description: OpenAI 发布预印本，称 GPT-6 系列模型仅凭推理和通用编码工具即可设计新蛋白的结构与序列，无需调用专用生物学模型。与 Onava 的实验室测试中，基于 GPT-6.2 设计的 minibinder 在 5 个靶点上均出现结合证据，322 个 minibinder 中 35 个（10.9%）结合阳性；重设计的抗体片段 66% 保留结合。  阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/yg04c9d5qnwzitqstg19c6ow2

items.title: 德国一消费者保护中心起诉 OpenAI，称 ChatGPT 订阅容易取消难
items.description: IT之家 11 月 26 日消息，据科技媒体 ComputerBase 今天报道，德国勃兰登堡消费者保护中心现已对 OpenAI 提起诉讼， 原因是 ChatGPT 订阅服务的取消流程过于繁琐 。 勃兰登堡消费者中心法律事务顾问 Dunja Neukamp 表示，要给 ChatGPT 开通订阅服务非常简单，只需要点几下按钮。然而反过来要取消，就没有那么简单。用户必须通过最初开通订阅的平台管理订阅服务，例如用电脑网页订阅的话，就无法用手机 App 取消。 该机构认为，OpenAI 并没有给退订留出足够的透明度， 且这种做法不符合德国法律要求 。 此外，该消费者组织还对 OpenAI 用户合同中的“需要时可以单方面调整订阅价格”提出质疑。他们认为这种条款不具备法律效力，因为 OpenAI 没有充分说明调整价格的合理依据。例如条款并未明确规定，只有在实际运营成本上涨时才能提高价格。

items.title: S&P considers Nvidia credit downgrade over governance and ‘key man’ risks
items.description: The credit rating agency may lower Nvidia's credit rating to AA-, the fourth-highest rating.
items.author: Marina Temkin
items.content: S&P Global Ratings, one of the three major credit rating agencies, is considering downgrading Nvidia’s rating, citing concerns about the company’s management and governance practices. Despite Nvidia’s strong financial performance, the ouster and reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang has raised concerns about “weak executive oversight and lack of succession planning” and “key man risk,” meaning heavy reliance on Huang for its future success, S&P said in a statement . The agency expects to finish its review within 90 days and could cut Nvidia’s rating from AA to AA-, the fourth-highest on its scale. Although Nvidia is certain to keep its investment-grade rating, a downgrade could raise its borrowing costs. Because Nvidia backstops neoclouds and other infrastructure companies that lack strong credit on their own, a lower rating could make their debt costlier or force them to post more collateral. In August, Nvidia announced plans to arrange $500 billion in financing for AI infrastructure with six financial institutions, including Goldman Sachs, Apollo, and Blackstone. Under the original terms, Nvidia would guarantee 25% of the loans. But even before Huang’s ouster and return, lenders had been demanding that Nvidia guarantee more, Bloomberg reported . A downgrade would likely prompt lenders to demand even larger guarantees.

items.title: Jensen Huang broke Nvidia’s code of conduct, and his employees may not forget it
items.description: Most codes of conduct serve as a reflection of corporate culture. In Nvidia's case, that could have consequences.
items.author: Russell Brandom
items.content: When Jensen Huang gave his first all-hands address since returning as CEO, there was an odd emphasis on Nvidia’s code of conduct. He admitted to violating the code, then emphasized that no one was exempt from it. But that “does not mean, the moment you violate a code of conduct, we walk you out the door,” Huang said, according to Wired . “Facts, circumstances, a lot of assessments” still matter. In other words, the code applies to everyone, but breaking it doesn’t automatically cost anyone their job, including, apparently, the CEO. It’s an awkward stance for a company whose CEO has admitted to breaking its rules. A central part of modern human resources, a code of conduct can seem like a quasi-legal rulebook that lays out unacceptable behavior. But experts say most codes are better understood as a reflection of corporate culture. When an infraction goes unpunished, the main risk isn’t legal but cultural — that employees will feel embarrassed or even angry about the company they work for. That’s the risk Huang now faces at Nvidia. The talks would mark a significant reversal from just two months ago, when Muse users discovered they were unable to purchase products on Amazon and instead received an error message when attempting to check out. According to a Wednesday report by Fortune , citing people familiar with the discussions, Amazon and Meta have held multiple rounds of talks about the matter. Two key issues remain under negotiation: how search results would be presented and how advertising would be handled under a potential agreement. One of Amazon’s biggest concerns is how third-party shopping agents like Muse could affect its advertising business. In October, Amazon CEO Andy Jassy argued that few customers were making purchases through outside shopping agents. Amazon may also have been waiting for Muse to mature before agreeing to integrate it with its marketplace. If Muse places the wrong order or creates a problem with a purchase, Amazon could ultimately be left dealing with frustrated customers and unhappy sellers. items.author: Lauren Forristal
items.content: Shopping with AI is becoming less of a futuristic idea and more of something companies expect us to do. Walmart is the latest retailer making that shift, teaming up with Meta to let customers shop its Black Friday deals through Muse, Meta’s AI agent. The partnership, announced Tuesday, gives shoppers another way to find products, compare prices, and make purchases without browsing Walmart’s website themselves. Instead, customers can simply tell Muse what they are looking for and let the AI do the work. The announcement highlights how differently Walmart and Amazon are approaching AI shopping. While Amazon has taken steps to stop third-party AI agents from making purchases for customers, Walmart is leaning into the idea. To get started, users open the Muse app, sign in to their Walmart account, and return to the assistant to begin shopping. They can ask it to find specific products, compare options, or track down deals. Once a customer makes a request in Muse, the assistant sends it to Walmart, which returns relevant products and helps build a shopping cart. Walmart says it has built privacy protections into the experience. For instance, Muse doesn’t get access to a customer’s Walmart shopping history or other personal information. Shoppers can also set spending limits, require approval before purchases, and review orders placed by the agent. Plus, the company notes users can always delete their agent’s profile if they want to.

items.content: Instagram users can now chat with Meta’s AI agent Muse in a DM thread, the company announced on Tuesday. The social media network says users can chat with Muse to get more context about a post, place, or product they come across, or catch up on conversations they may have missed in their other DMs. The new integration gets rid of the need for users to toggle between Instagram and the Muse app when they want to interact with the AI agent. It also reflects the growing competition among tech companies to make AI assistants a part of users’ everyday digital lives. By embedding Muse directly into Instagram, Meta is making it easier for users to access the AI agent, while also giving Muse access to a platform where users already discover products, places, and content. Users can share Instagram posts with Muse and ask it to take action, such as adding a coffee shop to their Mexico City itinerary or finding a Black Friday deal on a pair of shoes. Meta notes that conversations with Muse on Instagram will appear as a side chat in the main Muse app. Muse in Instagram DMs will begin rolling out on Tuesday for iOS and Android users in the U.S., Canada, Mexico, Japan, and Singapore. items.title: Tidal to ban and remove millions of AI-generated tracks as AI slop inundates music streaming
items.description: The company said it will still accept songs that were made with AI assistance, but not fully generated.
items.author: Ivan Mehta
items.content: Music streaming service Tidal said on Tuesday that it will start banning and removing songs generated fully with AI in a bid to stem the flood of submissions to its platform. The company said that over the past 90 days, more than 43% of tracks uploaded to its platform were generated by AI, and that was a major reason driving this decision. Tidal said it will start removing fully AI-generated music on December 9, and the process will result in more than 29 million songs being deleted from the platform by the end of the year. With the new rules in place, the platform said it will be rejecting roughly 80,000-85,000 tracks per day. Tidal is also banning distribution services from delivering 100% AI-generated tracks, and will reject submissions if songs’ metadata says they are made fully using AI. The company said it will still accept songs that were made with AI assistance, but not fully generated. The move comes as AI-generated music inundates streaming services across the board. Tidal is one of the first major platforms after Bandcamp to ban AI music outright . Deezer, which also provides detection tools to other streaming services , said that it will introduce a toggle to let users filter out AI music . Larger platforms like Spotify and YouTube Music have adopted a milder approach to this issue, choosing to label AI-generated music instead of offering filters or taking stronger measures. items.title: Why a Crusoe investor is betting on solar and batteries to power future AI data centers
items.description: Next-generation data centers will need tens of gigawatts of power every year. One of Crusoe's investors thinks solar and energy storage are the obvious choice.
items.author: Tim De Chant
items.content: The problem of supplying power to AI data centers has become one of the central debates of the AI era. In just a few years, the U.S. grid has gone from basically zero growth to adding several gigawatts a year. “Demand is growing faster than people appreciate,” Brook Porter, partner at G2 Venture Partners (G2VP), told TechCrunch. “It’s atoms, not bits, and the world is in the process of recognizing the realities of those challenges.” It’s been a bumpy road. Because it takes a while to scale supply chains, companies have been securing power in any form they can. In many cases, that has meant buying, renting, and deploying natural gas power plants , but Porter thinks that hyperscalers and data center developers should look at the bigger picture if they want to move faster. items.title: Three xAI founders want AI to predict the future
items.description: PLUS: How to put Microsoft Copilot to work
items.content: Good morning, AI enthusiasts, and welcome to our 3,907 new readers. Every AI lab trains on the internet. Three of xAI's founding members are taking that logic a step further, and they think it could be the answer to helping AI predict the future. Their new startup, Epochal, is giving AI agents a “time machine” to relive 30+ years of the web one date at a time — an experience they believe could unlock superhuman forecasters, and everything that comes with knowing what happens next. The Rundown: Three xAI founding members just launched Epochal, a startup building AI to predict real-world events, and debuted Time Portal, the first piece of what it calls a “time machine for the internet” that lets AI relive the web on dates going back 30+ years. Guodong Zhang, Zihang Dai and Manuel Kroiss are three of the five people named on the team, with Zhang reportedly putting in $100M of his own money. The company wrote that “Today's AI has read almost everything and lived through almost nothing,” and said it built Time Portal in just 90 days to fix that. The 1T+ page archive saves the busiest pages as often as once a minute, so agents can drop into a specific hour, not just a day, back in time.

items.title: Cybersecurity gets a $44B merger
items.description: PLUS: Nothing to launch its AI mystery product
items.content: Good morning, tech enthusiasts. Hackers spent the past few weeks breaking into banks, crypto platforms, and even supermarket fridges, some with the help of AI. Now the industry is consolidating to fight back, with CrowdStrike buying Zscaler for $43.9B in the biggest cybersecurity deal ever, aimed at protecting every device and connection under one roof. The Rundown: CrowdStrike is paying $43.9B in stock for Zscaler — the largest cybersecurity deal on record — to put the software guarding corporate laptops and the service screening their traffic under one company. CrowdStrike sells endpoint security — the software guarding laptops and phones. Zscaler sells cloud services that replace VPNs and screen traffic for threats. CEO George Kurtz says the deal opens a path to “the largest AI safety and security company the world has ever seen.” Cost cuts are pegged at $500M a year within 18–24 months of closing, with another ~$1B a year in added revenue projected inside 30 months.

items.title: Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia
items.description: PLUS: Go beyond the browser with the Claude desktop app
items.content: Good morning, AI enthusiasts, and welcome to our 3,697 new readers. The Jensen Huang saga already felt like a movie. On Monday, the scandal that had rocked the tech world for weeks hit its climax — the return. Jensen is back in the captain's seat at Nvidia, leather jacket and all, after President Donald Trump personally lobbied the board and its members voted unanimously to reinstate him. With it came $1T in market value, celebrations from the tech world, and fresh outrage on Capitol Hill. The Rundown: Nvidia's board just reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO only 11 days after he resigned over affairs with a direct report and a woman U.S. officials linked to Chinese intelligence, with President Trump saying he personally pushed for the return. The unanimous vote came six days after chair Harvey Jones ruled out rehiring Huang, with the board saying “senior levels” of the U.S. government weighed in. Huang said he takes the job back “with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” thanking interim CEO Colette Kress, who stays on as CFO. Trump told CNBC he'd been “speaking to the board directly and indirectly,” and posted that the government sees no reason to view Huang's return as a risk.

items.title: Nvidia’s robot king returns
items.description: PLUS: China's newest humanoid hits $1.6B
items.content: Good morning, robotics enthusiasts. Robotics’ post-Jensen Huang era lasted just 11 days. Nvidia’s board brought him back as CEO on Monday, likely a relief for the 35-plus robotics startups Nvidia has backed — especially the ones the company was calling to reassure while he was gone. Also: A Chinese humanoid startup wheels its way to a $1.6B valuation, and the UN ends a week of killer-robot talks by agreeing to two more years of talks. The Rundown: Nvidia’s board just put Jensen Huang back in the CEO chair, 11 days after he resigned amid a spy-and-affair scandal — and just as robotics insiders were sizing up a post-Huang era. Directors voted unanimously for the return, and input from senior U.S. government officials convinced them Huang poses no national security risk. Huang quit Nov. 12 over reported affairs — one with Alice Huang, an exec at Megaspeed, a company under investigation over alleged GPU exports to China. The gap briefly rattled robotics. Nvidia and venture arm NVentures called at least three portfolio startups to promise business as usual, while interim CEO Colette Kress had reportedly opposed some of Huang’s earlier deals. The company launched its Isaac robotics platform in 2017 and has since backed Figure, Neura, Skild, Wayve, and others, with Jensen often stepping on stage with cute little robots performing tricks by his side.

items.title: Claude helps solve math's biggest open problem
items.description: PLUS: Test Gemini 4 Neon on finding billing errors
items.content: Good morning, AI enthusiasts, and welcome to our 8,176 new readers. Few fields have changed more under AI this past year than math. Now, a single Anthropic mathematician and Claude may have solved a problem even the top minds thought was years, if not decades, away. Levent Alpöge says they just proved the Riemann hypothesis, a 167-year-old prime-number puzzle that carries a $1M Millennium Prize and has long been seen as math's most famous open problem. As with AI's other big math wins, not everyone is thrilled. The Rundown: Anthropic’s Levent Alpöge used Claude to crack the Riemann hypothesis, the 167-year-old question often ranked as math's biggest unsolved problem, after ~6 weeks of work, and checkers say it holds up, even as no human fully gets it yet. First posed in 1859, the problem asks whether prime numbers follow a predictable pattern, and the Clay Institute put a $1M “Millennium” prize on solving it in 2000. Alpöge shared the proof only as 17M lines of machine-checkable math, writing that Claude “flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line.” The groups behind Lean, the computer language used for verification, certified it on Saturday, saying they have “full confidence” that Alpöge’s proof is correct.

items.title: GTA 6 rakes in $2.4B overnight
items.description: PLUS: Google’s space data centers find a ride
items.content: Good morning, tech enthusiasts. Thirteen years of waiting, and Grand Theft Auto VI finally arrived this week — sending the internet into a frenzy. Tens of billions of clip views, nearly 8M concurrent livestream viewers, and hot takes flying from every corner of the gaming world. Count some of The Rundown staff among the hooked. The Rundown: Thirteen years and a $1B+ dev budget later, Rockstar Games’ Grand Theft Auto VI has arrived , generating $2.3B+ from preorders and launch-day sales and tying The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time as the highest-rated video game . Players switch between Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, an outlaw couple, across Leonida , Rockstar’s Florida stand-in. Vice City sits at its center, surrounded by beaches, swamps, and small towns. GTA 6 livestreams peaked at 7.91M concurrent viewers across platforms in the first hours of release, with peaks of 3.31M on Twitch and 3.22M on YouTube. The game’s so massive that the pre-download period set new records. At peak, one exchange handled the equivalent of ~13 game downloads per second.
